subject: Post-demo: SDK/SSO checklist and prompt-versioning playbook

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Post-demo: SDK/SSO checklist and prompt-versioning playbook

Hi Harper — great to meet today, and thanks for the demo time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have an actionable list for the tech follow-up.

TL;DR: Redwood can support the SDK flows and routing you asked about; next step is a 60-minute technical deep-dive with your infra lead to lock down auth and data residency.

What we covered (high level)
- SDK setup: lightweight JS/Python SDKs (client-side only) + server SDKs for token exchange.
- Auth options: API keys, short-lived JWTs via token-exchange, and mTLS/enterprise SSO for Private deployments.
- Routing: region pinning, SLO-based fallback, and per-route model selectors.
- Structured output & tool-calling: supported via explicit JSON schemas + tool descriptors (we showed a sample product lookup call).
- Embeddings & reranker: we recommend embeddings for semantic match, then a lightweight reranker (learned or score-combo) for top-K.
- Prompt governance: prompt versioning, immutable system prompt anchors, and red-team test harnesses for injection testing.

Open items / asks from FinEdge
1) Confirm technical point-of-contact for the deep dive (you mentioned an infra lead).
2) Expected throughput patterns (peak QPS and average document length) so we can size the Dedicated capacity suggestions.
3) Any data residency / logging constraints (SOC2/retention windows) — will influence routing & private options.
4) Clarify whether prompt mutability must be restricted to an approvals workflow (we can enforce via RBAC + signed prompt versions).

Attachments I’m sending
- redwood-arch-drawio.png (visual we referenced)
- prompt-templates-v0.3.json (sample prompt templates + system prompt metadata)

Proposed next steps
- Book 60-min deep-dive this week with your infra lead (Ben from our side will join).
- We’ll circulate a short SOW draft and an example reranker config for review.

Would Wednesday 10am PT work for your team? If not, please propose two slots.

Thanks — Tessa

Hi Harper / Tessa — Ben from the infra team here. Short technical notes ahead of the deep-dive so we can use the time for decisions, not education.

Auth & SDK
- SDK options: JS + Python + JVM clients that call your backend for token exchange. We support:
  * API keys (developer-friendly, long-lived)
  * Short-lived JWTs (recommended for production) via OAuth2 token-exchange (we can integrate with your IdP)
  * mTLS for Private deployments (if you want mutual TLS on the inference plane)
- SSO/SSO provisioning: SCIM provisioning + OIDC recommended; we can provide example claims including role and prompt-change rights.

Routing & residency
- Per-account routing rules can pin EU traffic to eu-west-1 and US traffic to us-west-2. We support automatic fallback to secondary region with per-route latency/cost policy.
- Audit exports: we stream structured usage logs (per-request metadata) to customer S3/GCS buckets or to your SIEM via syslog/endpoint.

Structured output & tool-calling
- We enforce schema validation at the SDK layer — model output is validated against supplied JSON schemas and a tool descriptor registry. Tool calls are emitted as discrete events and can be replayed or audited.

Embeddings + reranker
- We recommend a two-stage approach: approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) on compact embeddings, then a fine-grained reranker over top-50. Reranker options: lightweight logistic/ranker trained on your labels, or Redwood's default learned reranker. We’ve attached a small example config (reranker-config.yaml) you can use as a starting point.

Prompt governance
- Versioning: every system prompt is stored as a signed, immutable artifact (content hash + signer id). You can require a Doc-signed approval to move a prompt from staging to production.
- Injection mitigations: we recommend a layered approach — prefix anchors, response schema validation, tokenized context window monitoring, and periodic red-team tests (we can provide a red-team harness).
- Auditability: prompt change events are emitted into the audit stream with diff + signed author.

Pre-meeting asks for productive deep dive
1) Share a sample of the user query distribution (token histogram) and a couple of prompt examples (we’ll treat them as confidential).
2) Confirm whether FinEdge requires prompt change approvals to be via DocuSign or if an internal ticket + manager sign-off is acceptable.

I’ll be on the Wed 10am PT call. Tessa — can you send the calendar invite (Zoom preferred)?

— Ben
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
